column1: # Requirements for Mica::HTTP2's frame codec (milestone H2.1): the frame
# layer of RFC 9113 sections 3.4, 4, 6 and 7 (with the SETTINGS of RFC 8441
# and RFC 9218), and the plan's limits. Stream states and flow-control

column3: A server parser accepts the 24-byte client preface in any chunking and rejects a mismatch at its first differing byte (PROTOCOL_ERROR, connection)
The 9-byte header carries a 24-bit length, the type, the flags and a 31-bit stream identifier; the reserved bit is ignored on receipt and cleared on send
Frames of unknown types are skipped
Flags a frame type does not define are ignored and never sent
A frame longer than the advertised SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE raises FRAME_SIZE_ERROR as soon as its header arrives; a frame is never serialized over the peer's maximum
DATA carries data and END_STREAM; on stream 0 it is a PROTOCOL_ERROR
Padding as long as the payload or longer is a PROTOCOL_ERROR; a padded frame too short for its pad length is a FRAME_SIZE_ERROR
HEADERS carries a field block, END_STREAM, END_HEADERS, priority fields and padding; on stream 0 it is a PROTOCOL_ERROR; a self-dependency is a stream PROTOCOL_ERROR that still returns the frame
PRIORITY is 5 bytes (otherwise a stream FRAME_SIZE_ERROR), not on stream 0, and not a self-dependency
RST_STREAM is 4 bytes (otherwise a connection FRAME_SIZE_ERROR) and not on stream 0; unknown codes are kept
SETTINGS is on stream 0, a multiple of 6 bytes, empty when ACK is set (otherwise FRAME_SIZE_ERROR); unknown parameters are ignored

ENABLE_PUSH, ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL and NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES are 0 or 1 and MAX_FRAME_SIZE is 16,384 to 16,777,215 (otherwise PROTOCOL_ERROR); INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE over 2^31-1 is a FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR
PUSH_PROMISE carries a promised stream identifier (reserved bit ignored), a field block and padding, and is not on stream 0
PING is 8 bytes on stream 0 with ACK
GOAWAY is on stream 0, at least 8 bytes, with a last stream identifier, a code and debug data
WINDOW_UPDATE is 4 bytes (otherwise a connection FRAME_SIZE_ERROR); a zero increment is a stream PROTOCOL_ERROR on a stream and a connection error on stream 0
A header block continues only with CONTINUATION frames on its stream; any other frame, or a CONTINUATION outside a block, is a connection PROTOCOL_ERROR
All 14 error codes, and every FrameError carries its code and whether it is a connection or stream error
A header block passing max_header_block_bytes or max_continuation_frames raises FrameLimitError (ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM) when the frame that passes it arrives
Parsing a serialized frame gives the same frame, for random frames of every type
Bytes fed one at a time, or in random chunks, give the same frames and errors as the same bytes fed at once
A connection error sticks; after a stream error the parser goes on with the next frame
Random and mutated frame streams only raise Mica errors and the parser holds at most one frame plus the last chunk
